newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares ends with small gain, Eurotunnel down.
newsitem.headline: French shares ends with small gain, Eurotunnel down.

text.p: French shares closed with a gain on Tuesday, supported by the dollar which set fresh highs in the afternoon, dealers said.
However, remarks by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had hit the U.S. currency late in the morning, reducing Paris' opening gains.
The French market had been closed on Monday for Bastille day and catched up on Tuesday with advances on other European Bourses, such as London.
Eurotunnel fell by 9.27 percent at 6.85 francs, after strong gains last week on debt deal and following a strike announcement.
The CAC-40 index closed up 9.11, or 0.31 percent, at 2,950.7. CAC-40 July futures closed at 2,957 versus 2,950 at Friday's close.
The broader SBF120 index closed up 6.58 at 2,015.05
Total volume was 7.4 billion francs, of which 5.3 billion in CAC-40 shares.
SGS-Thomson led the risers, up 7.78 percent at 540 francs, on the back of better-than expected Motorola results last week and ahead of its first half results due on Thursday.
Defence electronics company Thomson-CSF closed 3.6 percent lower at 163.50 francs following the government's decision on Friday evening not to continue with the sale of the state's 58-percent stake.
